headline: Refined inference of tumor methylation, structural variants and clonal structure
label: Computational Tumor Genomics Methods
summary: Long-read, methylation and single-cell profiles are now paired with new inference methods to resolve tumor-specific signals in cancer genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is the recovery of tumor-derived signal from noisy or indirect sequencing measurements. CelFiE-ISH deconvolves ctDNA methylation from ultra-low-pass nanopore whole-genome sequencing, reporting a 1.7-3.1% cancer fraction detection limit. SVScope combines long-read evidence with local graph-genome optimization and random forests to improve somatic structural variant calling, reporting up to 23.64% F1 gain. scRevol applies reinforcement learning with a label-assignment strategy to single-cell RNA-seq copy-number profiles to infer tumor clonal structure and evolution. Each item reports gains in sensitivity, accuracy, or resolution. What is new is the extension of these inference problems to low-input and single-cell data. The items do not assess what the underlying models have learned or whether their outputs reflect mechanism.
